name: Progress bar
purpose: A DETERMINATE completion display: it shows how much of a known-length task is done, as a proportion of a known total. Linear (a horizontal rule that fills) and circular (a ring that sweeps). Use it whenever the remaining work is measurable — uploads, downloads, multi-part transfers, goal progress, completeness scores. When the remaining work is NOT measurable, use Loading indicator instead; this component has no indeterminate state by design.

props.name: shape
props.$note: Linear for inline/full-width progress in a flow; circular for a compact badge-like completeness score.

props.name: size
props.$note: Linear only: 4px rule (default) or 8px (emphasis). Circular is a single 96px specimen; further rungs need a ruling, not an invention.

props.name: value
props.$note: Current progress, on the min..max scale. Drives both the visual fill and aria-valuenow.

props.name: label
props.$note: The accessible name. Required — a bar with no name announces only a number.

props.name: valueText
props.$note: Human-readable value for AT (aria-valuetext). Required whenever the scale is not a plain percentage — e.g. '1,450 pounds of 2,000 pounds saved'.

props.name: showValue
props.$note: Renders the numeric value as visible text. Default TRUE and it is load-bearing, not decoration — see the contrast $finding: the numeric text is the meaning-carrier where the fill/track pair does not clear 3:1.

variants.name: linear
variants.use: inline or full-width progress inside a form, list row or card

variants.name: circular
variants.use: a compact completeness score where a full-width rule would not fit

variants.name: emphasis
variants.use: an 8px linear rule where the progress is the primary content of its region rather than a supporting detail

tokens.fill: progress/complete — Mono/Console #1A1A1A | #FFFFFF, Legacy #DB0011 both modes, Supercharge #B92F1E | #CC4333
tokens.track: progress/incomplete — #F0F0F0 | #484848 in Mono/Console/Legacy; #DFDEDC | #413934 in Supercharge (via the color/neutral -> color/warm DNA rebind, NOT an explicit override)
tokens.label: text/default @ t-cm-label
tokens.caption: text/secondary @ t-cm-caption
tokens.$note: Progress is STRUCTURE, not status (Dave 2026-07-21) — hence the ink pair in Mono/Console rather than a RAG colour. Legacy and Supercharge keep red fills by their own rulings.

dimensions.stackGap: 8px (gap/fixed/content) between label row and track — explicit because leading-trim is ON
dimensions.headGap: 12px between the label and the value in the head row

motion.fill: width (linear) / stroke-dashoffset (circular) transition at the standard ease, 140ms
motion.reducedMotion: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce removes the transition. The fill still MOVES to its final position — the value must remain reachable; only the animated sweep is dropped (2.3.3 / 2.2.2).

responsive.linear: The track is width:100% inside a max-width:420px column in the specimen; in use it takes its container's width. No breakpoint of its own.
responsive.circular: Fixed 96px; it does not reflow. Place it in a wrapping row rather than expecting it to shrink.

mustNotNeighbour: Loading indicator (showing both for the same task is contradictory — one claims the duration is known, the other that it is not)

accessibility.role: role=progressbar with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax on the element that represents the bar
accessibility.name: An accessible name is REQUIRED — aria-labelledby pointing at the visible label, or aria-label where there is no visible label
accessibility.valueText: aria-valuetext whenever the scale is not a plain percentage, so AT announces '1,450 pounds of 2,000' rather than a bare number
accessibility.circularNaming: On the circular form the role sits on the VISIBLE numeric caption and the svg is aria-hidden — the accessible name and the on-screen value are then the same object, and there is no duplicate announcement
accessibility.notColourAlone: The numeric value is rendered as text on every specimen. This is what satisfies 1.4.1 where the fill/track pair does not clear 3:1 (see $finding)
accessibility.motion: Animated fill respects prefers-reduced-motion; the final value is still reached
accessibility.passive: interactive:false — no keyboard interaction and no focus indicator by design. A progress bar reports, it does not accept input

antiPatterns: Using this for work of unknown duration — that is Loading indicator. There is deliberately no indeterminate variant here (s173-D1)
Relying on the fill/track boundary alone to convey progress — it does not clear 3:1 in Legacy dark or Supercharge dark. Always render the numeric value
Omitting the accessible name, which leaves AT announcing a percentage with no subject
Using aria-valuenow on a non-percentage scale without aria-valuetext, so AT reads '1450' with no units
Putting role=progressbar on a decorative svg as well as on its caption — the value is then announced twice
Adding a focus indicator or tabindex: a determinate progress bar is passive and must not sit in the tab order
Animating the fill without a prefers-reduced-motion block (fails the a11y gate)
REVIEW (inferred): rounding the track corners — border-radius/indicator resolves to 0 and the angular rule applies

tokenValidation.against: tokens/semantic-colour.json + tokens/layout.json + canon/canon.css four-theme cascade at HEAD be1e0a7
tokenValidation.result: PASS with one recorded FINDING. All six declared vars resolve cleanly in the mono base, light and dark. Three contrastPairs declared, each verified to hold in ALL FOUR themes rather than in the mono base alone.
tokenValidation.$finding: FILL-ON-TRACK DOES NOT CLEAR 3:1 IN TWO THEMES. progress/complete on progress/incomplete measures Mono 15.27 light / 9.15 dark PASS, Console identical PASS, Legacy 4.58 light PASS / 1.75 dark FAIL, Supercharge 4.48 light PASS / 2.38 dark FAIL. It is therefore NOT declared as a gated contrastPair (runbook step 3: a failing pair is a finding, carried another way, never declared as passing). Meaning is carried by the numeric value in text plus aria-valuetext. This is a PRE-EXISTING token-level condition — the same pair sits under the existing Progress-tracker bar — and is queued to _DS-IMPROVEMENTS.md, not fixed here: promotion is Dave's.
tokenValidation.$addressFinding: progress/incomplete carries NO explicit entry in any theme override file, yet resolves DIFFERENTLY in Supercharge (#DFDEDC / #413934) because its $alias targets color/neutral/13 and color/neutral/6 and Supercharge rebinds color/neutral onto color/warm. First-hand confirmation of the P-address class (#108): a token NAME is not an ADDRESS.
tokenValidation.$gateScope: knowledge/_validate_snippets.py resolve() reads tokens/semantic-colour.json only — the MONO base. It CANNOT observe the Legacy or Supercharge leg of any declared pair. The four-theme figures here were computed against canon/canon.css, outside the gate. Recorded so that a future reader does not mistake this gate's green for a four-theme green.

depricateUsage.note: None — progress/complete and progress/incomplete are live semantic tokens, not deprecated bindings.

tokenValidation.ignored: Spacing values (8px/12px/24px/32px gaps) follow the existing snippet convention of literal scale values; the manifest tracks colour, radius and motion bindings only.

provenance.$note: Built #174 as the first component through the scaffold route (s173-D1, Dave). No Figma node bound — this is a verified gap fill, not a Figma reconciliation. A design owner binds figma_node later.

A `progress-family` is therefore ARGUABLE — but arguable is not ruled, so nothing was minted here and component-types.json was not touched. Queued as a proposal for Dave.
